- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (1-3 days) after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral.  
- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.28 or below), model tends to ignore downward momentum and overpredicts recovery, leading to overshoots.  
- Forecasts show strong mean reversion bias — model assumes prices will stay high after peaks, but true outcomes often drop 5-10% within 5-7 days.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model forecasts a steeper continuation than actual, suggesting it underweights sentiment decay.  
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts — e.g., when sentiment turns negative, forecast doesn’t adjust downward until 3-5 days later.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates the “tail” of the price curve (last 5-7 days), especially when sentiment is weak or negative.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.06 or below), model tends to forecast higher prices than true outcome, suggesting it misinterprets sentiment as bullish.  
- Model exhibits lagged correction — it reacts to sentiment changes 2-3 days after they occur, leading to delayed downward adjustments.  
- Overshoots after spikes are most common when sentiment is positive and price is above 72.00 — model assumes momentum will continue, but sentiment fades quickly.  
- Model underweights sentiment in 30-day forecasts — it treats sentiment as a short-term signal, not a structural driver of long-term mean reversion.
